title: 37 War Elephants Over the Alps: Why Did Hannibal Take the Hardest Road?
summary: In 218 BC Hannibal marched an army and 37 war elephants from Spain to Italy, over the Pyrenees, across the Rhône and over the Alps in the first snow. Follow the march on real satellite maps as the army shrinks at every step, find out what really happened to the elephants, and see how the hardest road in the ancient world led to Cannae, and why it still was not enough to take Rome.
credits: Maps: NASA Blue Marble imagery (public domain) · Rivers: Natural Earth (public domain) · Ancient places: Pleiades (CC BY 3.0)
Ancient troop numbers are Polybius's and Livy's figures; modern historians often think the large ones are inflated
The route and the Alpine pass are approximate: nobody knows exactly where Hannibal crossed · Illustrations are drawn for this video, not real images
note:
Every frame is drawn with code on open map data. Where the ancient sources disagree, we tell you both.
